text:
Predicates:
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
MountainRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range.
LocatedIn(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
Donated(x) ::: x has been donated.
In(x, y) ::: x is in y.
InTexas(x) ::: x is in Texas.
InNewMexico(x) ::: x is in New Mexico.
InPicurisMountains(x) ::: x is in the Picuris Mountains.

Premises:
MountainRange(PicurisMountains) ∨ MountainRange(Texas) ::: The Picuris Mountains are a mountain range in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(JuanDeOnate, PicurisMountains) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
LocatedIn(HardingPegmatiteMine, PicurisMountains) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine is located in the Picuris Mountains.
Donated(HardingPegmatiteMine) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine was donated.
In(PicurisMountains, NewMexico) ∨ In(Texas, Texas) ::: The Picuris Mountains are in New Mexico or Texas.
In(Texas, Texas) ::: Texas has mountain ranges.
In(PicurisMountains, y) ∧ Mine(x) ∧ Donated(x) → In(y, z) ∧ Mine(x) ∧ Donated(x) (for some y, z) ::: If a mountain range in Texas has a mine that was donated, then it is in Texas and has a donated mine.

Conclusion:
In(Texas, Texas) ∧ In(PicurisMountains, Texas) ∧ MountainRange(PicurisMountains) ∧ In(Texas, Texas) → JuanDeOnateVisited(Texas) ::: If the Picuris Mountains are in Texas and Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains, then Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in Texas.
